heroHeadline: Junta's Operation 4926 Stalls in Rakhine as Resistance Strikes Air Base and Captures Karen Camp — Day 2,048
heroSubtitle: By Day 2,048 (September 11, 2026), the junta's multi-front Operation 4926 offensive against the Arakan Army in Rakhine State — launched September 4 across Sittwe, Ponnagyun, Kyaukphyu and border areas with Magway, Bago and Ayeyarwady — had stalled after nearly a week, with AA forces repelling junta columns near Warbo Island and Ponnagyun, recovering roughly 20 SAC bodies, and ISP-Myanmar assessing the AA now holds 92.6% of Rakhine State. Elsewhere, the Karen National Union captured the Tatmadaw's Htaw Mu Ple Meh camp in Papun District on September 8 after a 16-month siege, while Kachin Independence Army forces destroyed two more junta resupply vessels near Shwegu on September 9, bringing their river-campaign total to 14 vessels since late August. On September 10, People's Defence Force fighters struck Tada-U Air Force Base near Mandalay with six FPV drones — resistance sources claim four jets were damaged while the junta says all drones were intercepted — shutting Mandalay International Airport for two days, even as a retreating junta column killed five civilians, including a 90-year-old man, near Wedi village in Tanintharyi Region the same morning. A blast at an MNDAA explosives facility in Hsenwi Township killed or wounded at least 15 people, including two Chinese nationals, on September 8. On the diplomatic track, Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Phnom Penh on September 11 for a two-day state visit — his fourth ASEAN member-state trip since his April inauguration as president — meeting Hun Sen and Hun Manet despite renewed calls for his arrest under an outstanding ICC warrant request. AAPP data show 192 people killed by the junta between July 1 and September 8, 2026 (126 from airstrikes) and 82 people aged 65+ killed since the start of the year. AAPP's cumulative tally remains 8,335+ confirmed deaths since the 2021 coup, with 31,887 people arrested and 22,663 still detained or unverified; ACLED separately confirmed cumulative conflict deaths across all actors surpassed 100,000 in July. IDPs remain at approximately 5.2 million, with only 26% of the 2025 UN humanitarian appeal funded.
